questions.question: Explain how individuals and households put pressure on natural resources.
questions.expected_answer: Daily use: water, food (soil, water, fertiliser, energy), electricity (mostly coal in SA), transport fuel, manufactured goods, waste. Depends on wealth and lifestyle; richest use much more; SA highly unequal. Small actions add up: leaks, about a third of food (about 10 million tonnes) lost or wasted, landfills filling with plastic and organic waste. Choices shaped by prices, availability, public transport, electricity, recycling services.

questions.question: Define a carbon footprint and explain why it matters, with reference to South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Fossil fuels release CO2; greenhouse gases (CO2, methane) trap heat; enhanced greenhouse effect since Industrial Revolution; over 1 degree C warming; heatwaves, droughts, floods, sea-level rise; SA hotter and drier. Carbon footprint: total greenhouse gases from activities of a person/household/organisation/product/country, in tonnes CO2 equivalent per year; direct (petrol, gas) and indirect (electricity, food, goods, transport). SA about 6-8 t per person, world 4-5 t, USA more than double SA, many African countries under 1 t, due to coal and energy-intensive industry; inequality within SA; footprint calculators.

questions.question: Describe practical actions individuals can take, and explain the limits of individual action.
questions.expected_answer: Waste hierarchy: refuse, reduce, reuse, repair, recycle. Electricity: switch off, LEDs, geyser blanket/timer, efficient cooking, solar. Water: short showers, fix leaks, grey water, rainwater tanks, water-wise plants; Cape Town 50 L/day, use about halved. Food: plan, store, leftovers, compost, less red meat. Transport: walk, cycle, public transport, lift clubs. Shopping: reusable bags, less packaging and single-use plastic, durable/second-hand, SASSI, recycling (supports waste pickers). Schools. Limits: largest emissions from power stations, industry, mining, transport; lack of options; poor already low footprints, fairness. Governments: laws, renewables, public transport, recycling, plastic bag levy 2003, carbon tax 2019, Paris Agreement 2015; businesses: cut waste and emissions. Combined action needed.
